case.title: The most mysterious star in the galaxy (allegedly)
case.hook: Boyajian's Star: irregular dips of up to 22% that no planet could make. Aliens were proposed. Dust was found.

query.adql: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_over_error, pmra, pmdec, ruwe, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, bp_rp, phot_variable_flag, teff_gspphot, distance_gspphot, non_single_star, DISTANCE(POINT(301.5643860504275,44.4568863525439), POINT(ra,dec))*3600 AS sep_arcsec FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE 1=CONTAINS(POINT(ra,dec), CIRCLE(301.5643860504275,44.4568863525439,0.008333333333333333)) ORDER BY sep_arcsec

notes: rows_kept counts 6-month visits (W1 and W2), not exposures
observers (good points): HBB:29969, JSJA:16152, FJQ:10295, LPAC:9135, DFS:8273, HJW:7392, DUBF:6942, PXR:4743, GKA:3971, OAR:3679, BPAD:3576, ATE:3116
upper limits, discrepant (val=T) and non-standard bands are kept but flagged; visual estimates form their own series 'Vis.'
no ZTF source (target may be brighter than ZTF saturation, ~12.5 mag)
